File seals limit the set of allowed operations on a given file.
       For each seal that is set on a file, a specific set of operations
       will fail with  EPERM  on this file from now on.  The file is said
       to be sealed.  The default set of seals depends on the type of the
       underlying file and filesystem.  For an overview of file sealing,
       a discussion of its purpose, and some code examples, see
        memfd_create(2) .
